signal: CADDi raised a $38M Series C extension led by Atomico at a $470M valuation to grow its AI manufacturing data platform across the US.

email.body1:
Hiko, saw CADDi raised a $38M Series C extension led by Atomico at a $470M valuation to scale its AI data platform.

Scaling that fast across new markets usually means more in-market accounts than the team can cover before new hires ramp, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for CADDi off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress ~4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Hiko, quick follow-up for CADDi.

Post-raise, growth expectations jump faster than headcount can. Most teams don't know exactly how many meetings they need to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show how many meetings CADDi needs to close that gap, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Hiko, last bit of proof for CADDi.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks.

I pulled a benchmark of how CADDi's reply rate likely compares to peer Series-C startups. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
email.body4:
Hiko, I will stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. The stretch right after a raise is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a Series-C motion? I will tailor it to CADDi either way.
